newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace abandons Rockall as UK cedes claim.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace abandons Rockall as UK cedes claim.

text.p: Greenpeace called off its occupation of the tiny, barren Atlantic island of Rockall on Monday after Britain gave up its territorial claim to the outcrop.
The environmental pressure group successfully lifted off two activists who had spent 48 days in a "solar survival capsule" lashed to the storm-tossed rock.
Greenpeace claimed a partial victory in its bid to halt oil and gas exploration in the surrounding region of the Atlantic Ocean which it says will add to global warming.

Britain ceded its territorial claim to a vast area of sea covering 60,000 square miles lying beyond Rockall last week when the government signed a new U.N. treaty which forbids the use of uninhabited rocks as the basis for sovereignty claims.
James Hunt of the U.K. Oil Operators Association, which represents 40 oil companies operating off Britain's coasts, said oil and gas concessions could still be awarded in the area.
"We still have high hopes that this area can still be licensed even though Britain has given up its claim to ownership of the seabed there," he said.
"The key point is that undersea exploration for minerals, including oil and gas, does not depend on territory," he told reporters.

"Rather it depends on a judgement as to whether the geology of the sub sea rock is the same as that under the nearest territorial sea," he added. "We believe we have a good case for saying that it does."
Possession of Rockall, situated about 300 miles from the Scottish mainland, has been disputed by Britain, Ireland, Iceland and Denmark.
